newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs end a tad higher ahead of 10-year JGB tender.
newsitem.headline: JGBs end a tad higher ahead of 10-year JGB tender.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures ended slightly higher on Monday due to dealers' short-covering, traders said.
Investors were mostly inactive ahead of a 10-year JGB auction scheduled for Tuesday, traders said.

There was talk, however, that some investors had made profit-taking sales of 10-year JGBs between the 190th and 193rd issues and also medium-term JGBs, a trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Demand for the 10-year JGBs to be offered through Tuesday's auction will probably be moderate, traders said.

JGBs with 10-year maturities can be bought at under par in the secondary market, so there may not be as strong a demand for the new issues as was seen after recent auctions, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.

The Finance Ministry will probably leave the coupon rate for the new 10-year JGBs unchanged from the previous tender at a record-low 2.6 percent, and the issue amount is also likely to be unchanged at one trillion yen, traders said.
The March ended at 126.08, up slightly from the previous day's 125.97.
A strategist for Morgan Stanley advised investors to go long on Japanese stocks and short on the yen and Japanese government bonds in a recent report.

Barton Biggs, the investment bank's global strategist, said in a report issued on Friday that he expects the yen to remain weak "until the Japanese economy shows real signs of recovery and a resumption of inflation".
Biggs said in the report that as a strategy for investing in Japan he recommends "long stocks and short the yen and JGBs".
A trader for a city bank's securities unit said the report is unlikely to have much impact on the market.
Even if foreign traders sell based on the report, it is unlikely that domestic players will follow suit and sell in large amounts, the trader said.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.415 percent as of 0703 GMT, down from Friday's 2.420 percent.
